~Lick Wounds~.Effect: This should be on the pet feature and can heal.

Description:
As you evade an oncoming arrow, your focus shifts, leaving you vulnerable to the sudden onslaught of a raptor lunging at your throat. A whirlwind of steel and fang ensues, and as a sword is close to striking you, the attack suddenly stops. "You're no monster" he says as he unsheathes his sword, searching for tracks in the mud. "Best mind your own business, friend. The one I'm seeking is nearby... and it is seeking you."
Hunters are keen predators, who fight alongside one (or multiple) trusted beastly companions. While able to cast some rudimentary magic, spellcasting is not their focus, and they more than make up in terms of raw ferocity and power to kill.
A hunter can always navigate their surroundings, and can track down any monster, or person alike, no matter the scope.
Quick Note: Hunters are keen predators, who fight alongside one (or multiple) trusted beastly companions. While able to cast some rudimentary magic, spellcasting is not their focus, and they more than make up in terms of raw ferocity and power to kill.
Weapons: You are Trained in 2 Weapon Categories of choice (e.g. 1-Handed Melee, 2-Handed Ranged, Shields, etc).

Spellcasting.Change: You can change your known Spells and Talents inbetween Adventures.
Spellcasting.Other: All Hunter-specific Abilities are not considered Spells (unless stated otherwise).

Mana.Regain: As a Hunter, you don't use Mana. You rely on weapons, class Abilities and simple Basic Spells.

Spellcasting.Recommended Abilities Description: As a Hunter, your baseline kit with the pet and Class Abilities is very strong, but you are what some would call a "semi-caster" - a class with low access to magic and Abilities, so you need to work with what you've got! Resistance is a decent defensive option and Venin Shot might help dish out some more Damage. Cure Affliction can be amazing in certain niche scenarios, and Slam will help you deal with multiple opponents at once - just be careful not to slam into your allies!

~Animal Companion~.Effect:
You have an animal pet that can fight alongside you!
Your pet has the Stats 3, 1, 0, 0, -1 in any order, but they do not affect its Combat capabilities.
It has ^8 + 200% of Your Level^ Max Health.
It takes its Turn at the same time as you do (and always has the same Initiative as yours).
It has 1 Action per turn, which it can use to do its own Abilities or Pet Attack.

Instead of picking Level 1 Minor Talents for yourself, they apply to your Pet.
Also, choose 2 Level 1 - Pet Talents from below to give to your pet.
~Animal Companion~.Upgrade:
If your pet drops to 0 Health, it becomes Fallen, like a player. It has no Health Regen, but at any point outside of combat, you (the pet owner) can spend 30 minutes to tend to your pet's wounds and heal it back to full Health.
Your pet will not stray more than 30 meters away from you in hostile territory.
~Animal Companion~.Notes:
Your pet can make normal non-Combat Rolls using using its own Stats.
Your pet can't rise from being Fallen while in Combat, even if healed.
If your pet ever dies, you can spend 8 hours inbetween Adventures to get a new pet. If you want to change your Pet and abandon your current one, you can do so inbetween Adventures, but the guilt will make you Fumbling for the next 2 Worthy Combat encounters.

~Pet Attack~.Effect:
The pet melee attacks a target.
The attack deals 1d6 Pierce or Slash Damage (your choice).

~Tumble~.Effect:
Use when taking Damage (or any time on your Turn).
Roll 2 meters in any possible direction. Reduce the Damage by 50%.
~Tumble~.Upgrade: ^You^ can use this to make your pet tumble instead.

~Cure Affliction~.Effect:
Remove all combat-affecting Debuffs and Crowd Control on a Unit.
Also cure any non-chronic and non-terminal illness or disease on the Unit.
~Cure Affliction~.Upgrade: Alternatively, clean up to 2 rations or liters of water of microbes, mild poison or impurities.
~Cure Affliction~.Notes: Debuffs are things like curses, weaknesses, etc.

~Fake Sound~.Effect:
You create a sound out of thin air.
Make a Sense or Intelligence Roll (with no non-combat Skill) to determine its accuracy.
~Fake Sound~.Scaling: At Level 4, this lasts up to 1 minute. At level 8, this lasts up to 1 hour.

~Influence Beast~.Effect:
A non-Epic beast must make a Sense Roll at least equal to your Sense roll.
If it fails, you can change the beast's mood (make it hungry, afraid, nervous, etc).
The effect lasts 10 minutes, or until the end of its Turn if in Combat.

~Camping~.Effect:
Setup camp, creating favorable conditions for your party for up to 8 in-game hours.
Units in the camp are protected from all bad weather and are immune to being poisoned by food or drink.
Until the end of the Adventure, all Units who camped here are immune to Hard Terrain.

~Large~.Effect: Your pet is Large and occupies a 2x2 meter area.

~Ridable Steed~.Effect: Your pet is ridable as a mount and has +50% Movement Speed outside combat.

~Opposable Thumbs~.Effect: Your pet has opposable thumbs and can use Potions, Scrolls and other similar items.

~Flying~.Effect: Your pet can fly at its normal Movement Speed.

~Dig~.Effect: Your pet can dig and move through dirt as if it were just Hard Terrain.

~Wallwalking~.Effect: Your pet can walk on walls and ceilings at normal speed.

Other Abilities Description: Choose up to 2 Pet Talents to give to your pet. These are permanent and can only be changed by retraining your pet in later levels, via special Talents.

~Stand Proud~.Effect: If the pet ends its Turn without having dealt Damage, it heals for 1d4.

~Resilient~.Effect: Your pet is Large (2x2 meters) and has +6 Max Health.

~Grasping Talons~.Effect: If an enemy starts its Turn next to your pet, it is Slowed.

~Ambushing~.Effect: Your pet's first regular attack every Combat deals +1d6 Damage.

~Breath Attack~.Effect:
Choose an element.
Your pet's attack range becomes 4 meters and deals Damage of the chosen element Type.

~Antler Charge~.Effect:
Your pet has +1 Movement Speed.
If the pet moved at least 5 meters in a straight line, then attacked a target in front of it, Slam the target +1d4 Damage away from the pet.

~Spiky~.Effect: After a Unit makes an Attack on the pet from 1 meter away, the attacker takes 1d4 Pierce Damage.

~Venomous Attacks~.Effect: Your pet's attacks deal +1d4 extra Poison Damage to targets already affected by Crowd Control.

~Leaping~.Effect: Your pet leaps next to a Unit, Blinding it.

~Entrap~.Effect: Your pet entraps a Unit in web, goo or a similar substance, Rooting it.

~Grab and Throw~.Effect: Your pet picks up and Slams a Medium or smaller Unit up to 1d8 in any direction.

~Quillshot~.Effect: All Units within 3 meters of the Porcupine are shot with arrow-like quills and take 1d6 + 1d8 Pierce Damage.

~Lick Wounds~.Effect: Your pet heals a Unit near it for 1d12.

Starting Abilities Description.Animal Companion: As a Hunter, you always have your trusted Animal Companion with you.

Starting Abilities Description.Tumble: Tumble allows you to dodge-roll to avoid some of the Damage.

Specializations.Description: At Level 1, you can choose your specialization.
Choices: Draven, a tracker and hunter of beats and men, never lost and never without purpose
Beastmaster, a pack hunter, who finds friends in even the most ruthless of beasts

~Hunter Mark~.Effect:
Choose and ^Mark^ a target you can see.
Your own single target attacks and Abilities against the ^Marked^ target have their ^Dice Upgraded^ to the next die type.

~Tracker~.Effect:
You have +2 in Tracking (non-Combat Skill)
You always know where North is in non-magical environments.
You and your pets are unaffected by Hard Terrain.

~Infused Shots~.Effect: You can change your weapon attacks' Damage Type to {Type}.

<Pet Versatile Training>.Effect: When you get this Talent and at the end of every Adventure, you can change one of your pet's Pet Talents.

<Bola Shot>.Effect: After you Tumble, choose a 2x2 meter area and throw a net. Each Unit in the area take 1d4 Pulse Damage and is Slowed. If you rolled 4 for any of them, it is Rooted instead.
<Bola Shot>.Notes: Requires a Draven Net item, which can be bought for 50 gold (or freely crafted for the same price in materials). Can retrieved after every use.

<Bounty Hunting>.Effect: When your ^Marked^ target dies, you gain 1d100 {Gold}Gold and heal an ally within 6 meters for 1d8.
<Bounty Hunting>.Notes: Flavor-wise, you collect a trophy of your kill. The next time you are in a town, you redeem the Gold from selling the trophy.

<Slayer>.Effect:
You always know the type of a monster. You gain a different boon when ^you^ defeat a Worthy Enemy of a certain type:

{DarkGreen('Beasts:')} Heal an Ally for 1d4.
{DarkGreen('Demons:')} Your pet gains +1 Damage this Combat.
{DarkGreen('Fiends:')} Gain 50 {Gold}Gold.
{DarkGreen('People:')} Your next attack Cripples the target.
{DarkGreen('Undead:')} Your pet's next attack Single-Stuns the target.

<Pet Training 101>.Effect:
Choose one more Pet Talent.
While you have this Talent, your pet also has that Pet Talent.

<Bandage Wounds>.Effect: Heal a Unit for 1d4 for each 10 Health it is missing.

<Pet Versatile Trainings>.Effect: When you get this Talent and at the end of every Adventure, you can change one Pet Talent of one of your pets.

~Lance Heave~.DisplayRequirement: Only usable if it hits at least 2 Units
~Lance Heave~.Effect:
Make a {Weapon} ^weapon^ attack {Effect}
~Click on the Icon to select a preferred effect!~
~Lance Heave~.Combo: Comboed Units take the original full Damage.
~Lance Heave~.Notes:
Can apply weapon effects. If the weapon effect requires a target, applies to one chosen Unit hit.
Range increases do increase the length. The Damage must the same for all Units hit. All bonuses to the attack (e.g. Smite, Cursewielder, etc) also split evenly.

Variants.Name: Lance Heave
Variants.Effect: that hits all Units in a 3-meter long line. The Damage is evenly split among all hit Units.

Variants.Name: Blade Heave
Variants.Effect: that hits all Units in a 3-meter long line. The Damage is evenly split among all hit Units.

Variants.Name: Penetrating Heave
Variants.Effect: that hits one more Unit up to 2 meters directly behind the main target.

Variants.Name: Piercing Heave
Variants.Effect: that hits one more Unit up to 2 meters directly behind the main target.

<Crosshair Shot>.Effect:
Make an attack on a target.
For each meter to the target, the attack deals 1d6 Pierce Damage, up to 8 meters.
For each meter to the target over 8 meters, deal -1d6 Damage.
<Crosshair Shot>.Notes: At exactly 8 meters range, the attack deals 8d6 Damage. At 7 and 9 meters, it deals 7d6. At 6 and 10 meters, 6d6. And so on.

~Tag-Team Mark~.Effect:
Choose and mark a target you can see. ~Your Pet immediately dashes to the target and performs a Pet Attack if it's within 6 meters of the target.~
Your own ~and your pet's~ single target attacks and Abilities against the marked target have their ^Dice Upgraded^ to the next die type.

~Chaser Mark~.Effect:
Choose and mark a target you can see. ~If it's a non-Epic Unit, it is perpetually Single-Stunned while Marked.~
Your own single target attacks and Abilities against the marked target have their ^Dice Upgraded^ to the next die type.

<Pet Training 102>.Effect:
Choose one more Pet Talent.
While you have this Talent, your pet also has that Pet Talent.

<Treesposition>.Effect: Touch a piece of of a Large or larger piece of wood. Teleport near a similar piece of wood within 6 meters.

~Tree Stride~.Effect:
While within 30 meters of trees, you have +1 Movement Speed.
You can climb trees without making Rolls, using your normal Movement.
You can use as many meters of your Movement as you like to jump that distance from one tree to another.

<Tremor Wave>.Effect:
Shoot a thundering shot towards an obstacle or wall. A quaking wave travels horizontally towards in both directions of the wall up to 10 meters in each direction.
All Units within 2 meters of that wall must succeed a Might Check against 6 + ^Your Sense^ or be Triple-Stunned and take 3d4 Shock Damage.
They take half of the Damage and are Slowed if they succeed.
<Tremor Wave>.Notes: The floor and ceiling are not considered walls. The wave does not travel through them. This is considered a Spell. Ignores Cover.

<Improved Hunter Mark>.Effect: Hunter Mark makes your ^Dice^ further ^Upgraded^ to the next die type.

<Leafwalk>.Effect: You and your pet become ^invisible^. While a Unit is _leafwalking_, it heals for 1d4 whenever it does an Act. Lasts until the end of your next turn (or for 12 seconds if not in combat).

<Stat Bonuses 5>.Effect: Gain +1 in two Stats of choice, up to +5.

<Stat Bonuses 4 Extra>.Effect: Gain +1 in three Stats of choice, up to +4.

<Pierce and Cleave>.Effect:
When making a single-target attack on a Unit, your attack hits another target, depending on the weapon range:
{Diamond} If ranged, the attack hits the first Unit directly behind the main target within 3 meters of it, on a line, for 50% of the base Damage of the attack.
{Diamond} If melee, the attack hits one Unit of choice within 2 meters of the target, for 50% of the base Damage of the attack.

<Marked for Criticals>.Effect: After you use Hunter Mark (or an upgrade) on a target, it takes maximum Damage from the next dice roll.
<Marked for Criticals>.Notes: For example, after you Hunter Mark a Unit, if you attack it for 2d8 Damage, you don't roll; it just takes 16 Damage. Applies to bonuses like Dice Upgrades, Smites, etc.

<Eye of the Hawk>.Effect:
All enemies in a Worthy Combat are automatically _Marked_, and your range increases by 500% and your ^Dice^ are further ^Upgraded^ to the ^next^ die type against _Marked_ Units. After manually casting Hunter Mark, your first attack deals 50% more Damage against that Unit.
You automatically pass all Hard Dexterity Checks (that require at least 15) and your Sense and Dexterity increase by an extra 2.

<Eye of the Raptor>.Effect:
Your attacks deal maximum Damage to Units that are not _Marked_ if they are within 3 meters of you or your Pet.
You automatically pass all Hard Sense Checks (that require at least 15) and you gain +3 Sense.

~Prowl Around~.Effect: You have +2 to all non-Combat Sense Rolls.
~Prowl Around~.Notes: This is because of your Animal Companions roaming about.

~Stablemaster~.Effect:
You have 3 different Animal Companion pets, but only one can adventure with you at a time.
Each of your Animal Companions has 2 Pet Talents, and you can distribute your Minor Level 1 Talents among your pets as you like.

While not with you, your other Animal Companions hang out on their own in the wilderness, but no more than 5 kilometers away from you.
You can send your current companion off, then spend 30 minutes to call for another one to come join you.
~Stablemaster~.Notes:
The advantage is you can use several animal Abilities that have longer Cooldowns; these are usually stronger.
It is possible that the animal you're calling can't come to your aid if you're indoors, flying or the trail you're on is too difficult. In that case, you will have to return outside or on a safe trail (QM's decision).
In that case, your current companion can not go away, either.

<Pet Versatile Trainings>.Effect: When you get this Talent and at the end of every Adventure, you can change one Pet Talent of one of your pets.

~Infused Bites~.Effect: You can change your pet's attacks' Damage Type to {Type}.

<Kindred Spirits>.Effect:
One more of your Animal Companions accompanies you while adventuring.
This Animal Companion obeys the same rules as the regular one (takes its turns, requires healing between combats, etc).
<Kindred Spirits>.Notes: You're instantly kicked from the group if your pets don't have names.

<Singular Apex>.Effect: Each of your Animals now has 4 instead of 2 Pet Talents, +100% Health and deals 2d6 Pet Attack Damage instead of 1d6.

<Double Training>.Effect: Teach each of your Animal Companions one more Pet Talent.

<Pet Versatile Training>.Effect: When you get this Talent and at the end of every Adventure, you can change one of your pet's Pet Talents.

<Ravage!>.Effect:
One pet makes a melee Attack for 5d6 Slash Damage.
If the target is at or below 50% Health, deal 2d6 extra Damage and the target halves all healing it receives for the rest of the encounter.
<Ravage!>.Notes: This takes 1 Action from YOU, not your pet.

<Sickem>.Effect:
Use when a Unit goes flying against its will on someone else's turn.
Your pet(s) within 5 meters of its landing place can dash to it (after it lands) and make a total of 2 Pet Attacks on it.
<Sickem>.Notes:
Goes flying means is pushed, knocked up, dragged, etc.
This uses YOUR Reaction, not your pets'.
Obviously, the pets need line of sight and can't jump through walls, or over large obstacles. Apply common sense.

~Search~.Effect:
Name or describe a Unit that is familiar to you. Your animals go and search for your target.
They point which direction (straight) the target is.

~Camouflage~.Effect:
You and all your pets (if any) become camouflaged and turn effectively invisible and causing no sound, undetectable by the naked eye.
While camouflaged, your Movement is halved.
You appear, however, in mirrors, reflections and in recordings (as well as your sounds).

<Coordinated Bite>.Effect: One enemy near each of your pets (and/or summons) becomes Single-Stunned, Blinded and Slowed.

<Call To Action>.Effect: Call to one more of your animal companions! It appears from the wilderness and fights for up to 1 minute as if it were a normal Animal Companion.

<Second Winds>.Effect: Instantly heal yourself and all your pets for 3d6.

<Stat Bonuses 5>.Effect: Gain +1 in two Stats of choice, up to +5.

<Shapeshifting Pet>.Effect:
Turn one of your pets into a different animal type from the `Pets and Animals page$/Other/PetsAndAnimals`. If it's enhanced by a Talent, it keeps all enhancements (e.g. from Large Double).
Passively, your Pets gain +3 in all Stats, +10 Health, +2 Movement Speed and +1d4 Damage on all attacks.
<Shapeshifting Pet>.Upgrade: If you have the Wild Single Talent, you can turn a pet into a combination of 2 Animals.

<Cryptid Tamer>.Effect:
One of your Animal Companions becomes a Beast, Dragon or Insect from the `Monsters page$/Other/Monsters` worth less than 500 XP. It doesn't have a regular Pet Attack, but it has exactly the Abilities and attacks, but only 50% of its Max Health. It obeys the rest of your Animal Companion rules as normal.
Passively, your Pets automatically pass all Very Hard Sense Checks (requiring at least 20).
